title: Sebastian and the Thorn
premise: Wren Brightwater has spent his life hiding the beast-speaker gift that got his mother burned, guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains while pretending to be ordinary. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin receiving answers, Wren discovers he is the vessel chosen to carry the gods' returning memory — a secret that both the last loyalists of the old faith and the king's witch-hunters would kill to possess. Hunted through the passes with a dying god's voice in his head, Wren must choose between burying the old gods forever and revealing his true self to the world. In the end, he speaks — to beasts, to crowds, to the sky — and the old gods return not as conquerors but as equals, while Wren finally belongs to himself.
about_author: Mara Halloran is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six years leading mule trains through mountain ranges that inspired Thornfell. She writes fantasy about outsiders who find their place in wild, half-remembered worlds.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren guides a smuggler caravan through the Thornfell passes, concealing his gift even from the mules' easy trust in him. At a wayside shrine, an old woman's desperate prayer is answered by a voice no one else hears — and it speaks Wren's name. The chapter establishes his isolation and ends on dread: the silence he built his life around has broken.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The voice belongs to Vaelith, a dying old god who names Wren her vessel of memory. Witch-hunters arrive in the valley asking about answered prayers, forcing Wren to flee with Vaelith's fragment riding his mind. His childhood friend Sera catches him mid-escape and sees the truth of his gift. The emotional beat is terror giving way to the first fragile relief of being known.

chapters.title: The Price of Carrying
chapters.summary: POV alternating Wren and Sera. Pursued through high passes, Wren learns carrying Vaelith erodes his own memories — she is consuming his identity to survive. Sera must decide whether to help him reach the gods' ancient seat or turn him over to save her village. Betrayal looms when hunters offer amnesty for Wren's capture; Sera chooses him, and they fight free as Vaelith's presence surges toward climax.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Thorn
chapters.summary: POV Wren. At the ruined heart-shrine of Thornfell, Wren learns 'Sebastian' was the god's first vessel — a man erased for hiding. Offered the same erasure or open revelation, Wren chooses to speak aloud before gathered villagers and hunters alike, releasing Vaelith to return freely rather than inside him. The old gods wake as neighbors, not masters, and Wren stands unhidden at last.
